answer: Sybil resistance can work through staked identity bound to a physical wharf: each agent must register a hardware quill that signs every epoch from a unique island node, and the stake is slashed if two identities ever sign from the same node. An attacker must then buy and physically place one quill per fake identity, plus lock matching stake, so forging a thousand sybils costs a thousand devices and a thousand bonds—making the attack economically irrational.
